title: Resonantly Enhanced Phonon Transport by Magnon Pumping in a Ferromagnetic/Piezoelectric Bilayer
authors: André José, Carlos Eduardo, Adrielson Dias, José Araújo, José Holanda
abstract: We report the first experimental observation of resonantly enhanced propagating phonon transport induced by magnon pumping in a ferromagnetic/piezoelectric bilayer. Surface acoustic waves (SAWs) generated in a 128$^{\circ}$ Y-cut LiNbO$_3$ delay-line device resonantly excite magnetization dynamics in an adjacent Co film through magnetoelastic coupling. The enhancement of the transmitted acoustic signal occurs exclusively when the SAW frequency satisfies the ferromagnetic resonance condition predicted by the Kittel dispersion, providing a direct experimental fingerprint of resonant magnon-phonon coupling. A systematic comparison between the Co/LiNbO$_3$ bilayer and the bare LiNbO$_3$ substrate demonstrates that the observed transmission enhancement originates solely from the dynamic interaction between propagating phonons and coherent magnetization precession. Furthermore, measurements performed at different SAW harmonics reveal that only the harmonic satisfying the FMR condition produces a measurable enhancement, confirming the frequency-selective nature of the phenomenon. These findings establish an efficient mechanism for transferring energy from magnons to propagating phonons and provide a new strategy for actively controlling coherent acoustic transport in hybrid spintronic, straintronic, and quantum phononic platforms.
summary: The researchers experimentally observed that propagating phonon transport in a ferromagnetic/piezoelectric bilayer is significantly enhanced only when the acoustic wave frequency matches the ferromagnetic resonance frequency of the magnetic film. This confirms a direct, resonant energy transfer mechanism from magnons to phonons, establishing a new method for actively controlling acoustic energy flow using magnetism.
main_problem: To experimentally demonstrate and investigate the phenomenon of resonantly enhanced propagating phonon transport induced by magnon pumping in a ferromagnetic/piezoelectric bilayer.
main_result: The enhancement of the transmitted acoustic signal occurs exclusively when the SAW frequency matches the ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) condition, confirming resonant magnon-phonon coupling.
method: The study measures the SAW transmission coefficient ($S_{21}$) spectrum while sweeping the external magnetic field, comparing results on the bilayer versus a bare substrate.
model_or_system: The physical system is a Co/LiNbO3 hybrid bilayer. The interaction mechanism relies on magnetoelastic coupling between propagating Surface Acoustic Waves (SAWs) and the magnetization dynamics of the Co film.
key_observables: The enhanced transmitted acoustic signal ($\Delta S_{21}$) measured as a function of the applied magnetic field and SAW harmonic.
important_parameters: The SAW frequency must satisfy the Kittel dispersion relation for the Co film's FMR condition.
main_assumptions: The observed enhancement is solely due to the dynamic, resonant interaction between propagating phonons and coherent magnetization precession.
figures_summary: Figures show the device schematic, the measured SAW transmission spectrum ($S_{21}$) highlighting the resonance, and comparisons showing that only the SAW harmonic matching the FMR condition exhibits the enhancement.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical setup, uses FMR measurements to predict the resonance condition (Kittel fit), and then measures the SAW transmission, demonstrating that the enhancement is localized precisely at the predicted resonance field and is frequency-selective.
why_interesting: This work provides a direct experimental realization of energy transfer between magnetic excitations (magnons) and mechanical waves (phonons) in a controlled, resonant manner, which is highly relevant for understanding coupled quantum systems.
